content:
Hi all,

I'd like to announce formal-mathfin, a Lean 4 library of machine-checked mathematical finance, built on Mathlib and @Rémy Degenne 's BrownianMotion.

The motivation is a gap. Mathlib's probability and stochastic-calculus APIs are still thin, and continuous-time pricing theory is essentially unformalized. formal-mathfin aims at a comprehensive, honest reference for the field, and along the way builds reusable measure-theoretic and Itô-calculus infrastructure on top of the existing libraries.

It currently has 287 theorems across 11 areas: Black-Scholes with the full Greek matrix and the PDE, the exotics, Merton jump-diffusion, binomial trees with American / Bermudan / Snell envelope, fixed income with hazard credit, first-to-default baskets and Vasicek SDE, portfolio theory from Markowitz to Black-Litterman, coherent risk measures, Kelly, mortality, and constant-product AMMs. A few results:

  • the Black-Scholes PDE derived from the risk-neutral expectation via Feynman-Kac and heat-kernel differentiation, independent of the closed form and of Itô
  • the n-step CRR binomial price converging to the Black-Scholes call (characteristic functions + Lévy continuity + put-call parity)
  • a from-scratch L² Itô formula, f(B_T) - f(B_0) = ∫₀ᵀ f'(B_s) dB_s + ½∫₀ᵀ f''(B_s) ds
  • the equivalent martingale measure as a theorem, constructed from the physical measure by a static Girsanov / Esscher tilt; the discounted asset is then a proven Q-martingale

On standards: there is no sorry and no project-local axiom anywhere. Every full derivation depends only on the three Mathlib standard axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound), and the load-bearing ones are #print axioms-pinned as a build invariant. For every theorem the library states exactly what is proved and what is assumed: 270 of the 287 are full derivations or thin Mathlib wrappers, and the remaining 17 are honest reduced cores. Builds on Lean v4.31 / current Mathlib.

The work is strongly AI-assisted: an agent does much of the proof engineering, but every definition and theorem statement is human-reviewed, and the axiom audit is the enforced honesty floor.

Public artifacts, all linked from the README: the paper (arXiv:2606.01356, q-fin.MF), a Zenodo DOI, and a Hugging Face theorem dataset.

Feedback, bug reports, and contributions are very welcome.

Repo: https://github.com/raphaelrrcoelho/formal-mathfin
Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.01356
cc @Saverio Lidonnici @Mert Ünsal
